result.title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
result.summary: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed \emph{motion collapse}, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. On VE-Bench, the evaluated composite reward prefers a motion-suppressed candidate in $97\%$ of cases. Learned video rewards and a VLM judge also struggle with mild suppression, while latent optimization and reward-guided fine-tuning exploit this weakness to increase reward as motion declines. A linear probe of our base reward backbone performs near chance on mild suppression, motivating an explicit inter-frame dynamics input. We propose a motion-aware reward model that combines an RGB frame-difference stream with preference training against motion-suppressed and fabricated-motion negatives. A distillation anchor preserves alignment with human quality judgments. On the VE-Bench motion ladder, our model reduces the rate of selecting motion-suppressed candidates to $0\%$ while achieving a Spearman correlation of $0.57$ with human quality ratings. It also detects unseen suppression variants and preserves motion during reward-guided fine-tuning on two editing pipelines. These results support explicitly modeling motion in rewards for video editing.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究指令引导视频编辑奖励模型的「motion collapse」：用受控的运动抑制变体诊断复合奖励、学习式视频奖励与 VLM 评判均偏好退化候选，并提出融合 RGB 帧差流、以运动抑制与伪造运动为负样本做偏好训练的 motion-aware 奖励模型，辅以蒸馏锚点保持与人类判断对齐。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但其「代理奖励偏好退化输出、并可被 latent 优化与微调利用」的诊断及帧差显式动态输入，可能为 latent 推理中视觉证据保留、奖励/验证器设计与退化状态检测提供可供核查的线索。
